# ISO 10993 — Biological Evaluation of Medical Devices (Series)

> _Demo content — not for clinical use._ This is a **demonstration** applicability analysis for the PainEase PCA Advanced (PP3500). It records how the ISO 10993 biological-evaluation series maps onto this device program; it is not a controlled biocompatibility record and cites fabricated demo design inputs / hazards.

**Standard**: ISO 10993 series — *Biological evaluation of medical devices* (parts -1, -5, -10, -23 in scope for PP3500)
**Category**: Biocompatibility / Biological Evaluation
**Recognized by FDA**: Yes — several parts FDA-recognized (some partially). See the registry distillation for editions and recognition scope.
**Registry distillation (what the standard says)**: [`.claude/skills/medtech-docs/references/standards/iso-10993.md`](../../../.claude/skills/medtech-docs/references/standards/iso-10993.md) — the L1a finding aid with the series overview, the (contact category × duration) endpoint framework, the FDA recognition table, and the 2021 -10/-23 split. **Cite both** this applicability file and the L1a distillation when answering ISO 10993 questions for PP3500.

## Overview

ISO 10993 governs the biological evaluation of the PP3500's patient-contacting and user-contacting materials. Part 1 frames the evaluation as an activity within the device's ISO 14971 risk-management process; the numbered test-method parts supply the endpoint methods (cytotoxicity, sensitization, irritation). For PP3500 the evaluation is driven by a **limited-contact, intact-skin / indirect-blood-via-fluid-path** contact profile, which triages to the "big three" screen: cytotoxicity, sensitization, and irritation.

## PP3500 Applicability

**Contacting materials in scope** (per DI-011):
- Patient-contacting materials of the **dedicated administration (PCA) set** — indirect blood contact via the fluid path.
- **Lockbox exterior** surfaces.
- **User-interface surfaces** (touchscreen / housing the user contacts).

**Contact classification** (per DI-011): **limited contact**; **intact skin** for user/patient surface contact; **indirect blood contact via the fluid path** for the administration set. Under ISO 10993-1 this profile selects the cytotoxicity / sensitization / irritation endpoints as the primary screen `[VERIFY exact endpoint set against ISO 10993-1 Annex A / FDA guidance matrix]`.

## Finding — edition-dependence of the "-10 = sensitization/irritation" attribution `[VERIFY]`

Both DI-011 and HAZ-011 attribute **cytotoxicity/sensitization/irritation testing to "ISO 10993-5/-10"** — i.e., they fold irritation into **ISO 10993-10**. Per the L1a distillation, that attribution is **edition-dependent**:

- **ISO 10993-10:2010** — *Tests for irritation and skin sensitization* — covers **both** irritation and sensitization. Under this edition, "-10 = sensitization/irritation" is correct.
- **ISO 10993-10:2021** — retitled *Tests for skin sensitization* — sensitization **only**. Irritation was split out to the new **ISO 10993-23:2021** (*Tests for irritation*).

**Action for the DHF:** pin the ISO 10993-10 **edition** wherever the biocompatibility endpoints are cited. If the program follows current (2021) editions, the **irritation** obligation should cite **ISO 10993-23:2021**, and the DI-011 / HAZ-011 acceptance criteria should read "cytotoxicity per ISO 10993-5, sensitization per ISO 10993-10, irritation per ISO 10993-23" rather than "-5/-10". If the program deliberately relies on the :2010 edition (e.g., recognized-edition or transition rationale), record that decision explicitly. This is a citation-accuracy fix, not a change to the tests themselves — the "big three" screen is unchanged; only the *part number attributed to irritation* moves. `[VERIFY]` the edition the PP3500 program intends to conform to, and confirm the FDA recognition status of the chosen editions.

_Note: the demo currently cites parts **-5 / -10** per the DI-011 acceptance criteria; this file does not rewrite DI-011 or HAZ-011 — it flags the edition-pin as the open item._
